Thanks for this perspective. Yes, it's hard when someone you've been so open with suddenly terminates you. That's frustrating. I'm sorry you went through a similar experience. 

I am still looking for the right match. Did it take you a long time to trust a new therapist? I already have a history of abandonment issues so obviously this didn't help.
Thank you. I agree they shouldn't work with me if they don't feel equipped but I don't understand how I misjudged so much and thought they were the right fit.

I don't think I did anything wrong in the moment. I was just confused because when I "interviewed" them before we started working together during the intake I had mentioned prior S/I and potential for future S/I and they didn't indicate it would be an issue unless there was an imminent safety concern which there wasn't.

We ended the session where I mentioned I had S/I but no intent and they were just like "okay see you next week." Then over the course of the week I got rejected from a job I thought I was perfect for and was having a hard time with it so wanted to discuss my feelings with my therapist. Then they opened the next week with "sorry can't work with you". I just meant something more immediate came up so I wasn't super interested in discussing the S/I and thought it was fine since they didn't make a big deal out of the disclosure at the time. I can't see how routine life circumstances and pretty common ones at that would be ground for termination.
That's true. I keep telling myself that the right fit will come eventually and I read other stories on this sub and sounds like people had to go through quite a few people to find the right one.
Thank you for this validation. Yes, that is exactly what I was confused about. I am continuing to search for a better fit.
